validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: gem.wiki was 403/Cloudflare-blocked this run and wiki_citations.json is empty for this scope, so I went straight to open-web / primary-source research, per the scope note. Found SSGC's own official 'Gas Transmission Capacities Utilization' capacity table (https://www.ssgc.com.pk/web/?page_id=5597, dated as-of 2018-06-30 but still the live page on ssgc.com.pk) which lists, under subsystem A3-1 (Shikarpur to Quetta), a line item reading verbatim '12\"/18\"/20\" dia. x344 Km Quetta Pipeline' with capacity 90 mmscfd. This is an EXACT match on all four numeric GEM fields simultaneously (length 344 km, diameter set 12/18/20 in, capacity 90 MMcf/d, and the line is explicitly SSGC's, i.e. Owner1=SSGC). Independently, Dawn (2025-11, https://www.dawn.com/news/1955372) and The News International (https://www.thenews.com.pk/latest/1358208-gas-supply-disrupted-in-quetta-after-major-pipeline-rupture) both report a live 2025 rupture/repair event on 'a high-pressure transmission pipeline of SSGC' near Mach (on this exact corridor, between Sibi and Quetta), describing an '18-inch diameter QPCEP pipeline' rupture and a parallel '12-inch QPL line' used as backup to feed suburban Quetta -- independently corroborating that a real, currently-operating, SSGC-owned, multi-diameter (12in and 18in confirmed by name; 20in only in the SSGC table) transmission pipeline physically exists on the Jacobabad/Shikarpur-Sibi-Mach-Quetta route in 2025. Business Recorder (https://www.brecorder.com/news/40192782, verified 200 + 'Quetta'+'Mastung' present via url_verifier, though WebFetch itself 403'd so I could not quote its text) reports SSGC restoring gas to Quetta, Mastung, Kalat & Pishin on the same corridor, consistent with the same system. Net: 2+ independent sources (SSGC primary table; Dawn/TheNews secondary reporting) agree on existence, operator, transmission classification, and multi-diameter construction -- existence is solid, not a hallucination. CLASSIFICATION: correctly a transmission line -- SSGC's own document title is 'Gas Transmission Capacities Utilization' and Dawn/TheNews both describe it explicitly as a 'transmission pipeline' / 'transmission line', not a gathering/feeder line. PipelineType=transmission confirmed. DUPLICATE CHECK vs roster: the only other roster entry serving Quetta is P4022 Zarghun-Quetta Gas Pipeline (61 km, 12in, 25 mmscfd). The SAME SSGC table separately lists, under subsystem A3-2 ('Zarghun to Quetta'), a line of exactly 12in dia / 61 km / 25 mmscfd -- an exact independent match to P4022's own GEM values. This confirms P4021 and P4022 are two distinct, separately-documented physical corridors feeding Quetta from different directions (Jacobabad/Sui system vs. the Zarghun gas field) -- NOT a duplicate/relabel of each other. No other roster row plausibly overlaps this route. ATTRIBUTION: Owner1=Sui Southern Gas Co (SSGC) 100% confirmed both by the SSGC table itself (it is literally SSGC's own transmission-capacity report) and by Dawn/TheNews naming SSGC as the operator dispatching repair crews. StartLocation=Jacobabad/Sindh and EndLocation=Quetta/Balochistan match the SSGC table's own line label 'Jacobabad-Quetta Main Line' and general geography (Quetta is Balochistan's capital). SPEC: Length 344 km, Diameter '12, 18, 20' in, Capacity 90 MMcf/d all match the SSGC primary source exactly (verified via url_verifier with tokens '344'+'90' and 'Jacobabad'+'Quetta', both OK). No material spec disagreement found. One thing flagged as a caveat rather than a concern: news coverage of the 'Quetta Pipeline Capacity Enhancement Project' (QPCEP) cites region-wide capacity figures of 149->200->226 mmscfd, which is much higher than GEM's 90 mmscfd -- but that figure is the aggregate post-enhancement supply capacity for the WHOLE Quetta system (this line + several separately-named loop lines + added compressor stations at Sibi/Shikarpur), not this one line's own base design capacity, so it does not contradict GEM's 90 mmscfd for this specific 344 km line. Overall verdict: confirmed with that documentation caveat, no data errors found.

Do not confuse with the higher 149/200/226 mmscfd figures reported for the region-wide post-QPCEP supply system -- those aggregate multiple lines plus compression, not this line alone.
